examples.solution_text:
(a) Move each digit one column left. The $2$ ones become $2$ tens.
$2.684\times10=26.84$
(b) Move each digit two columns left. The $7$ hundredths become $7$ ones.
$0.079\times100=7.9$
(c) Move each digit one column right. The $6$ ones become $6$ tenths.
$6.53\div10=0.653$
(d) Move each digit two columns right. The $4$ tens become $4$ tenths.
$48.7\div100=0.487$

examples.question_text:
Choose the missing value.
(a) $0.064\times\square=6.4$, using $10$ or $100$.
(b) $3.82\times\square=0.382$, using $\tfrac{1}{10}$ or $\tfrac{1}{100}$.
examples.solution_text:
(a) The $6$ moves from hundredths to ones: two columns left.
$0.064\times100=6.4$
$\square=100$
(b) The $3$ moves from ones to tenths: one column right.
$3.82\div10=0.382$
$\square=\tfrac{1}{10}$

examples.question_text: A decimal becomes $7.36$ after it is multiplied by $10$. Find the original decimal and check it.
examples.solution_text:
Reverse multiplying by $10$ by dividing by $10$.
$7.36\div10=0.736$
Check: $0.736\times10=7.36$

examples.question_text: Which is greater: $10$ times $0.508$ or $100$ times $0.053$? Show both values.

examples.solution_text:
Move each digit two columns left. The $3$ hundredths become $3$ ones, and the $6$ thousandths become $6$ tenths.
$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c} & \text{Ones} & \text{Tenths} & \text{Hundredths} & \text{Thousandths} \\ \hline \text{Before} & 0 & 0 & 3 & 6 \\ \hline \text{After} & 3 & 6 & 0 & 0 \end{array}$
The decimal point stays between the ones and tenths columns.
$0.036\times100=3.600=3.6$
